reading.body:
A single OpenStreetMap record in Aulla, Italy, tagged as a data center, is more plausibly a small fixed-wireless ISP's equipment site than a colocation facility.

The record carries zero megawatts, no operator, and no confirmed business registration. Its name, Wi-Fi Communication Aulla, points to a wireless internet provider, and the town sits in the Lunigiana area of Tuscany where wired broadband is less developed. A base station or network operations point for that kind of provider is real telecom infrastructure, but it is not the same thing as a commercial data center leasing capacity to outside customers.

For AI specifically, this tells almost nothing. The binding constraints on AI scaling are power and the buildings that house dense compute, and a facility with no stated load, no operator, and no confirmed identity cannot be counted against either. The nearest airport, Sarzana-Luni, is 8.4 miles away, which is the only other concrete fact in the record and does not bear on compute capacity.

What the data does not cover is the actual nature of the site. The research status is exhausted, meaning the operator's website was never checked against the entry, and the only source is a tagging review. Treat this as an unverified point on a map, not as a data center in any sense that matters to AI infrastructure.
